children: The U.S. Treasury's intake of corporate taxes declined significantly in its fiscal year ended Sept. 30, 2026, as the Trump administration's signature tax reform took hold.

Corporation income taxes fell to $381.4B for the full fiscal year 2026 from $452.1B in FY 2025, according to the U.S. Treasury Department's monthly statement. The One Big Beautiful Bill, passed by the Republican-controlled Congress last year, allows corporations to claim larger deductions for new investments.
That helped contribute to the country's swelling federal deficit of $1.99T for the year, up 12% Y/Y.
By contrast, income taxes from individuals increased 7.2% to $2.85T from $2.66T in the prior year.

Tariffs added $173.2B into the government's coffers, down from $194.9B in FY 2025, as the administration was forced to restructure its tariff regime after the Supreme Court ruled that tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act weren't legal.
Higher interest rates also contributed to the higher deficit. Interest on debt paid during the fiscal year grew to $1.36T from $1.22T, according to the data.
